        <div class="welcome-header">
          <h1>AffineDrift</h1>
          <p class="subtitle">Scientific Notes on Golf Mechanics, Modeling, and Control</p>
        </div>

        <div class="welcome-intro">
          <p>
            AffineDrift is a technical research portfolio on golf swing mechanics, multibody dynamics, and nonlinear control. It collects textbook-style chapters, source maps, reproducible model links, validation notes, and critique responses so that claims can be read with their assumptions and evidence in view.
          </p>
          <p>
            The established material is the mathematics and mechanics literature behind the models. The AffineDrift contribution is the golf-specific application, synthesis, and review workflow: some pages are polished exposition, while others remain exploratory hypotheses or implementation notes.
          </p>
        </div>
      </section>

      <!-- Math Showcase -->
      <section id="framework" class="math-section" style="margin-top: 3rem;">
        <h2>The Core Framework</h2>
        <p>Several pages model the golf swing as a control-affine system:</p>
        <div class="math-showcase">
          $$\dot{x} = f(x) + g(x)u$$
        </div>
        <p>
          Where <em>f(x)</em> represents the drift dynamics (passive forces including gravity and velocity-dependent inertial coupling terms) and <em>g(x)u</em> represents the controlled torque inputs from the golfer.
        </p>
        <div style="margin-top: 1rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: var(--bg-secondary, #f8f9fa); border-left: 3px solid var(--primary-color, #2563eb); border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-light, #6b7280);">
          <strong>Provenance:</strong> The control-affine form ẋ = f(x) + g(x)u is standard in nonlinear control theory (Isidori, 1995; Nijmeijer &amp; van der Schaft, 1990). Its application to golf biomechanics — the drift/input decomposition, ZTCF, and DCR — is AffineDrift synthesis. See the <a href="articles/theory-part1.html">Theory Part 1</a> derivation and the <a href="critiques/index.html">Critiques &amp; Responses</a> for scope limitations.
        </div>
      </section>

      <!-- Verification and Review Section -->
      <section id="verification" class="approach-section" style="margin-top: 3rem;">
        <h2>Verification and Review Workflow</h2>
        <div class="approach-content">
          <p>
            AffineDrift prioritizes artifacts that can be inspected: equations, citations, executable model links, validation reports, issue-linked review notes, and CI results. Syntax checks, tests, and repository inventories help catch mechanical errors, but they do not convert exploratory biomechanical interpretations into established results.
          </p>
          <p>
            Computational tools support drafting, refactoring, and repeatable checks. Scientific claims still have to be tied to stated assumptions, cited sources, model code, or explicit numerical experiments.
          </p>
          <p>
            Not every page is at the same editorial stage. Some pages are polished expositions, while others remain exploratory notes or literature-review scaffolds and should be read with the status notes on each page in mind.
          </p>
          <p>
            Critical review is part of the publication model. Limitations, objections, and unresolved evidence gaps are surfaced alongside the main articles in dedicated "Critics' Comments" sections, rather than hidden behind them.
          </p>
        </div>
      </section>
